items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: A.J. Johnson went into the Southern Centipaders. And it was the same person.

ctx.x: There was a band called the Southern Serenagers. Did you ever hear of them?

The Southern Melody Boys or the Southern Centipaders? It could have been any name. Both of them. There were two. Southern Melody Boys and the Southern Centipaders. And who were they? Millard McNeil. And he had the Southern Melody Boys. A.J. Johnson went into the Southern Centipaders. And it was the same person. I'll just change the names there.
And where were they from? San Antonio. I see. I think that's the band that made a record with them. They just didn't know anything about them.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1969-12-30
items.q: The musicians that would know him would be like A.J. Johnson and he's past.

ctx.x: Well, the history behind him is kind of vague. I don't know of too many people that can recall Edgar Perry. Some of them in San Antonio do recall him and they remember him playing and leaving. The musicians that would know him would be like A.J. Johnson and he's past.
So there's just a band that disappeared from the scene. That's right. Maybe you could find something in California or something.

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-12-30
items.q: Well, A.J. was from here, I mentioned him to you yesterday.

ctx.x: Well, A.J. was from here, I mentioned him to you yesterday. And he has a sister that's still playing, she's up in age, but she does it short. A.J. Johnson. Yes, Clayton Johnson was her sister. A.J. was with the original, uh, McNeil Southern Sync papers.
